title: How to Set Financial Goals and Track Your Progress in Nepal
metaDescription: A proven framework for setting SMART financial goals in Nepal. Align household budgets, children's education funds, and retirement plans with NPR milestones.
h1: How to Set Financial Goals and Track Your Progress
directAnswer: To set and achieve financial goals in Nepal, divide objectives by time horizon: short-term (1-2 years: emergency reserve, holiday fund), medium-term (3-5 years: vehicle purchase, business seed capital), and long-term (5-15+ years: home purchase, children's higher education, retirement). Attach precise NPR figures and target dates to every goal to monitor trajectory quarterly.
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.contentHtml:
A goal without a timeline and an NPR target is merely a wish. Structure your family's objectives into three distinct horizons:

Short-Term (1 - 2 Years)

Funding a 6-month emergency buffer (NPR 300k - 500k), clearing credit card liabilities, or saving for family Dashain expenses. Hold strictly in Class A bank savings accounts.

Medium-Term (3 - 5 Years)

Accumulating a 30% down payment for a residential apartment or land purchase, or funding startup capital. Utilize recurring bank fixed deposits and high-grade corporate debentures.

Long-Term (5 - 15+ Years)

Funding children's university tuition and personal retirement independence. Utilize disciplined monthly contributions to Citizen Investment Trust (CIT), SSF, and broad index portfolios.

Schedule quarterly reviews on Ashoj 31, Poush end, Chaitra end, and Ashad 31 to check if your actual savings rate matched targets. If market fluctuations or living cost inflation created variance, re-balance allocations proactively. Discover our goal-based financial planning for personalized assistance.

faqs.question: How do I account for inflation when setting long-term goals in Nepal?
faqs.answer: Nepal's historical consumer price inflation averages around 6-7% annually. When forecasting expenses 10 years out (such as university fees), assume purchasing costs will approximately double.
